 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Jaylen Brown says the Philadelphia 76ers , owners of the best record in the Eastern Conference, have a clear leader.
 And it's not LeBron James , the NBA's all-time scoring leader and four-time NBA champion.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "[Tyrese] Maxey's been leading the way, 100%," Brown told reporters via John Clark of NBC10 Philadelphia . "He's been here, this is his team. Him and Joel [Embiid] have been here for a while, so the mindset has been to compliment those guys. I'm finding my footing, but Maxey's been leading the way for sure."
 The 6-foot-2 Maxey, a former first-round pick out of Kentucky, has scored 26+ points in every game as the new-look Sixers have forged a 7-1 record, including two wins over Jalen Brunson and the defending NBA champion Knicks. Maxey is averaging 29.1 points, third-best in the NBA, 5.3 assists and 4.1 rebounds. His 11.0 points per game in the fourth quarter ranks first in the NBA.
 The Sixers acquired Brown in a blockbuster deal in July when they traded away 36-year-old Paul George along with two first-round and two second-round picks for a player who was just outside the NBA MVP conversation last season. The trade was widely viewed as a huge win for the Sixers, with ESPN's Mike Wilbon calling it "insane."
 After adding Brown to a core that included Maxey, Embiid and star rookie V.J. Edgecombe, the Sixers then signed James to a two-year, $8 million deal in free agency.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement At just $4 million this season, the soon-to-be 42-year-old James (a billionaire already) has been a huge addition for the Sixers, averaging 16.2 points, 7.3 assists and 7.0 rebounds.
 James said he chose the Sixers - after having "visions" of playing for the Knicks - in part because of his relationship with Maxey, who is also represented by Rich Paul of Klutch Sports.
 "First of all, my relationship with Tyrese Maxey goes beyond the court," James said in September on the " Mind the Game" podcast with Steve Nash .
 Before Maxey first became an All-Star in 2024, James admired the passion with which Maxey played.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I just love everything about Tyrese Maxey, man," James said. "Every day you get the same person, and that is very rare in sports and it's obviously super rare in life. I've always talked about how great of a person he is. And we obviously know what he brings to the basketball court.
 "When I became a free agent and we decided to let the Lakers know that I wouldn't be returning, he was one of the first people that was on my line. 'Yo, what are we doing? What's up, OG? What's up, old head? Come on down here, man. We could use you down here.' … There's a lot of times that I don't answer the phone for some phone calls, because I don't even want to be swayed one way or I already know what you're calling about. But he's such a great person. I cannot not talk to him."
 James first met Maxey ahead of the 2020 NBA Draft, where the Kentucky product was the 21st pick.
 "He's been the same person since the moment I met him, before he was drafted into the NBA," James said. "The same exact person. He came to my house and at that point in time he was 19 years old, so he was actually hanging with (my sons) Bronny and Bryce. They were playing video games inside the house. So I met him and said what's up to him when he was going into the draft. But he was closer to Bronny and Bryce than he was to me, so he was hanging with them.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "He came in and he was super respectful to me, super respectful to my wife, super respectful to everyone in the house. Bright smile and just super down to earth. From the moment he's gotten drafted to the perennial All-Star, superstar that he's becoming, nothing has changed. Nothing has changed in his demeanor.
 "And we all know how people can be the humble kid coming in, and then some success happens and they're totally different. The kid has been the same person, man. It's hard sometimes, too. I'm not faulting anyone for having some change. … But this kid — this young man now — is beyond his years for sure."

 It's now fair to ask if James leaving the Lakers for the Sixers in free agency has benefited both teams.
 Led by an offensive early-season onslaught from Luka Doncic, the Lakers are 6-2 while the Sixers are 7-1 heading into Wednesday night's game with the Detroit Pistons (6-1).
 And Tyrese Maxey is leading the way.
